{{short description|German physicist}}
'''Günther Dollinger''' (born 2 August 1960 in [[Kempten im Allgäu|Kempten]]) is a German [[physicist]] and [[professor]] at the [[University of the Bundeswehr Munich]].

== Life ==
Dollinger completed his doctoral studies in physics at the [[Technical University of Munich]] (TUM). He is currently head  of the Institute of Applied Physics and Measurement Technology within the Faculty of [[Aeronautics]] and [[Astronautics]] at the [[University of the Bundeswehr Munich]].<ref name="LRT2-en 2022">{{cite web | title=Univ.-Prof. Dr. rer. nat. habil. Günther Dollinger | website=LRT2-en | date=4 April 2022 | url=https://www.unibw.de/lrt2-en/team/dollinger | access-date=17 July 2022}}</ref> He conducts research in different interdisciplinary and interinstitutional research projects. He is a member of the Munich Centre for Advanced Photonics, an inter-university excellence cluster, funded by the German government,<ref>http://www.munich-photonics.de/1/menschen/members/member/?personid=34&cHash=d277f75f55 {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727065517/http://www.munich-photonics.de/1/menschen/members/member/?personid=34&cHash=d277f75f55 |date=2011-07-27 }} Dollinger's profile at the Munich Centre of Advance Photonics</ref> based at [[LMU Munich]].

== Awards ==
For his doctoral [[dissertation]] titled ''Carbon film as a stripper for heavy ions'' Günther Dollinger was awarded doctoral and postdoctoral price of the Association of Friends of the Technical University of Munich.<ref>{{cite web |title=Promotions- und Habilitationspreise 1990 |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131021061643/http://www.bund-der-freunde.tum.de/index.php?id=113 |website=Bund der Freunde der Technischen Universität München |language=de |date=2013-10-21 |access-date=2025-08-11}}</ref>

In January 2025, Günther Dollinger received the MLZ Prize for “Instrumentation and Scientific Use” for his work on the positron source at the Heinz Maier-Leibnitz Zentrum (MLZ). Dollinger's working group developed the PLEPS (pulsed low-energy positron system) instrument as one of the central devices at the MLZ positron source.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MLZ Award for Shooting Star Prof. Günther Dollinger |url=https://www.frm2.tum.de/frm2/news-single-view/article/mlz-preis-fuer-shooting-star-prof-guenther-dollinger/ |website=Heinz Maier-Leibnitz Zentrum |access-date=2025-08-11 |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Together with his team at the Institute of Experimental Physics of the TUM in [[Garching]], Günther Dollinger developed a new type of [[microscopy]] methods for material analysis. For the first time it allows the three-dimensional analysis of the distribution of [[hydrogen]] in microstructured samples.

== Personal ==
Dollinger is married, lives in Garching near [[Munich]], and is the father of former beach volleyball players Sebastian and Armin Dollinger, as well as another son who works as a math and physics teacher.
